title: Classic AI: search, planning and rules
hook: Rule bases, search, planners and solvers. When no learning is needed at all.
inPlainWords: Before machine learning, AI meant programs that search through options or follow expert rules. Those methods are still the right answer when the rules are known and mistakes are costly.

useCase.title: Plan tomorrow's delivery for 40 vans and 900 parcels
useCase.story: Each van has a size limit and a driver shift. Parcels have delivery time windows. ShopEase wants the cheapest set of routes that keeps every promise. Nothing needs predicting: the rules and distances are known.

approaches.name: Hand-written rules (expert system)
approaches.what: Experts write if-then knowledge into a rule base.
approaches.greatWhen: Rules are clear and stable, and you must explain every decision.
approaches.avoidWhen: Rules are huge or change constantly.
approaches.example: If a parcel is fragile and heavy, use the padded van.

approaches.name: Search
approaches.what: Explore possible steps to reach a goal, the way a map app finds a route.
approaches.greatWhen: There is a clear goal, known moves and known costs.
approaches.avoidWhen: There are far too many options to try without shortcuts.
approaches.example: The shortest road from the warehouse to one customer.

approaches.name: Heuristic search
approaches.what: Search guided by a rule of thumb about which options look promising.
approaches.greatWhen: Big search spaces where a good-enough answer is fine.
approaches.avoidWhen: You need a guaranteed best answer.
approaches.example: A route finder that prefers main roads.

approaches.name: Constraint solver (optimization)
approaches.what: State the rules and the goal, and the solver finds the best plan that obeys the rules.
approaches.avoidWhen: The inputs are uncertain or unknown.
approaches.example: Assign 900 parcels to 40 vans within their time windows.

approaches.name: Planning
approaches.what: Work out an ordered list of actions that reaches a goal.
approaches.greatWhen: Robots and workflows where actions and their effects are known.
approaches.avoidWhen: The world changes unpredictably in the middle of the plan.
approaches.example: Pick, pack, label, load, in the right order.

approaches.name: Learning-based approach
approaches.what: Learn a strategy from data or from a simulator.
approaches.greatWhen: The rules are unknown but you have lots of examples.
approaches.avoidWhen: The rules are known. Just compute the answer.
approaches.example: Predict traffic delays, then feed them to the solver.

challenge.question: The rules and distances are known, and you need the cheapest valid routes. What fits?

options.why: It finds a plan that provably obeys every rule and can be re-run when inputs change.

options.text: A neural network trained on last year's routes
options.why: It may break time windows or overload vans, and nobody can see why.

options.text: Ask a language model to plan the routes
options.why: It cannot guarantee that the rules are obeyed.

options.text: A manager draws the routes by hand
options.why: Fine for five vans. It falls apart at 900 parcels.

bestCase.title: Compute what you can compute, and learn only what you cannot
bestCase.example: A solver builds routes that respect every van limit and time window. A small ML model predicts tomorrow's traffic delays, and those predictions feed into the solver as inputs.

worstCase.title: Learning what you could simply compute
worstCase.example: A neural network trained on last year's routes suggests a plan that overloads two vans and misses ten delivery windows. Nobody can tell why, and there is nothing to fix except more training.

steps.label: Parcels, vans, rules
steps.goes: Sizes, shifts and time windows become the constraints.

steps.label: Predict delays (ML)
steps.goes: A small model estimates traffic for each area.

steps.label: State the goal
steps.goes: Minimize total driving, and never break a promise.

steps.label: Solver searches plans
steps.goes: It finds the cheapest plan that obeys every rule.
steps.goesWrong: A neural network guesses routes with no guarantee that they obey the rules.

takeaway: If the rules are known and must be obeyed, compute the answer. Use learning only for what you cannot compute.
